listenings.text: You asked about my Tuesday, so here it is, and it is not exciting. I wake up at half past six and I leave home at twenty past seven, because the first class starts at eight and I hate arriving late. Classes until midday. Then I usually eat something on campus with the same two people, always the same table. In the afternoon I have a group project, and on Tuesday I never go to the gym. I go three times a week, but never on Tuesday, because by six o clock I am finished. What does a normal Tuesday look like for you?

Good morning, everyone. A quick note about the schedule. Starting next week, the statistics class moves from Thursday to Wednesday at eight in the morning. I know. Eight. It is not my decision. The room changes as well: it is room four zero two, same building, one floor up. And because the class moves, the deadline for the second assignment moves too, one week later, to the twenty-ninth. Please update your calendars today, not the night before. Thank you.

items.situation: Someone asks what your week is like. Answer with three sentences and one frequency word.
Ask me two questions about my week.
Describe your brother's week — not yours. Careful with the S.
You have three deadlines this week. Say how you are going to manage.
Say one thing you always do and one thing you never do on a Friday.
